requested_changes.body:
This string comparison is brittle. It only matches when `def.protocol.source` is exactly `"^https?$"`, which means:

- `z.url({ protocol: /^https$/ })` still accepts `https:example.com` (I verified this)
- `z.url({ protocol: /^http$/ })` still accepts `http:example.com`
- Any alternative regex spelling like `/^(http|https)$/` won't get the fix

A more robust approach would apply the `://` check whenever any protocol constraint is set, not just for the specific `httpUrl()` case. Something like:

```ts
if (def.protocol && !trimmed.includes('://')) {
  // reject
}
```

Or at minimum, use a regex test instead of string comparison:

```ts
if (def.protocol && /^\^https?\$$/.test(def.protocol.source)) {
```

The capturing group `([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*)` is unused. If you only need to verify `://` presence, a simpler non-capturing pattern suffices:

```ts
const hasAuthority = /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//i.test(trimmed);
```
